title: Speed up SHAP importance and calculation; sync uv.lock after #295
body:
## Description
This PR combines the SHAP speed-ups with a lockfile fix. Every change except the last bullet leaves results unchanged.

- **SHAP importance aggregation** (from ing-bank/probatus#294): faster `calculate_shap_importance` in `probatus/utils/shap_helpers.py`.
- **Single model parse:** `shap.Explainer`'s automatic selection parsed each tree model twice, once only to check support. Tree models are now built with shap's tree algorithm directly. Linear models are still checked first, as shap does, and other models fall back to the automatic selection.
- **Parallel SHAP:** new `n_jobs` on `shap_calc`, `ShapModelInterpreter` and `DependencePlotter`; `SHAPImportanceResemblance` now uses its existing `n_jobs` for SHAP. The default background-sample (interventional) tree SHAP is single-threaded and holds the GIL, so rows are split across processes. Each row depends only on itself and the background sample, so values are bit-identical. The default stays `n_jobs=1`. `ShapRFECV` is unchanged here because its folds already run in parallel.
- **Documented faster option:** `feature_perturbation="tree_path_dependent"` was already accepted. Its docstrings now describe it as the faster choice for tree models and note that it gives slightly different SHAP values. It stays opt-in. A new notebook, `docs/discussion/nb_shap_feature_perturbation.ipynb`, compares both options on a LightGBM example:
  - single SHAP calculation ~30× faster, `ShapRFECV` ~6× faster;
  - SHAP values correlate at 0.99;
  - the top 10 features keep their rank;
  - feature elimination removes the same features in every round.
- **Regenerated `uv.lock`:** upstream #295 changed `pyproject.toml` without it, so `uv run --locked` fails on main. The package set changes only by probatus 3.1.5 → 3.1.6, plus numba 0.62.1 and llvmlite 0.45.1, which apply only to Python >= 3.14 on x86_64 macOS.

## Type of change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue): lockfile out of sync with pyproject.toml
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality): faster SHAP aggregation and calculation, `n_jobs` for SHAP
- [x] Documentation update: docstrings and a comparison notebook

## Checklist:
- [x] My code follows the code style of this project.
- [ ] My change requires a change to the documentation/notebooks.
- [x] I have updated the documentation or added a notebook accordingly.
- [x] I have tested the code locally according to the **CONTRIBUTING.md** document.
- [x] I have added tests to cover my changes.
- [x] All new and existing tests passed.

## How Has This Been Tested?
Run locally:
- `uv lock --check` passes.
- `scripts/check.py --locked` passes lint, types and docs; tests: 177 passed, 11 skipped. One more fallback test was added afterwards; it passes on its own and lints clean.
- The new notebook was executed and saved with its outputs. It passes the pre-commit hooks (nbQA mypy, ruff) and renders in `mkdocs build`.

Results unchanged:
- The new `shap_calc` was compared against the previous commit across LightGBM, XGBoost, random forest, decision tree, CatBoost and linear models. This covered binary, multi-class and regression models, NumPy and DataFrame input, categorical data, both SHAP modes and `n_jobs` 1 and 4. All 54 combinations gave bit-identical values and expected values, or raised identical errors.
- The full workflows below produced identical reports before and after.
- The new tests assert that parallel and serial results match for each class, and that a tree model is parsed once.
- Separately, the new `calculate_shap_importance` matched the old one bit-for-bit on 11,726 generated inputs. It differs only when the penalty is disabled and SHAP values are infinite or overflow; that feature now sorts first instead of last, where the old order came from a NaN sort key.

Timings: 4 vCPUs, LightGBM 100 trees, best of 2 runs, with the previous commit as baseline:

| Workflow | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `ShapModelInterpreter`, 7,500 train + 2,500 test rows, `n_jobs=4` | 53.2s | 15.0s (3.5×) |
| `SHAPImportanceResemblance`, 2,500-row test set, `n_jobs=4` | 19.3s | 6.2s (3.1×) |
| `ShapRFECV`, 5,000×100, `tree_path_dependent`, `n_jobs=1` | 60.0s | 54.1s (−10%) |
| `ShapRFECV`, opt-in `tree_path_dependent` vs default (3,000×40) | 61s | 10s (~6×, values differ slightly) |

The first parallel call in a process is slower while joblib starts its workers.

## Additional Context:
- `tests/feature_elimination/test_feature_elimination.py::test_complex_dataset` flaked once in about 9 full runs. It is also flaky on main, so this change doesn't cause it.
- Not addressed here: `ShapModelInterpreter` with default settings failed shap's additivity check on a plain LightGBM model during benchmarking (SHAP values summed to −3.438, model output −3.516).

title: Speed up SHAP importance aggregation with measured benchmarks
body:
## Description

SHAP importance aggregation calculated standard deviations even with the default disabled variance penalty, then built, converted, sorted, and discarded a temporary report column. Skip the unused variance calculation, construct only the public report columns, and release the full multiclass absolute-value array after reducing over classes.

Repeated measurements against `d07a6b0`, using the same locked Python 3.12 environment, show:

| Workload | Before | After | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| SHAP aggregation, 100 × 20 float64 | 0.319 ms | 0.194 ms | 1.64× |
| SHAP aggregation, 20,000 × 200 float64 | 15.101 ms | 4.144 ms | 3.64× |
| SHAP aggregation, 20,000 × 200 float32 | 5.743 ms | 2.410 ms | 2.38× |
| Multiclass aggregation, 3 × 5,000 × 100 | 3.533 ms | 2.124 ms | 1.66× |
| Fitted `ShapModelInterpreter.compute()` | 14.068 ms | 6.895 ms | 2.04× |

Peak traced allocations for the large float64 aggregation fall from 61.1 to 30.5 MiB. Enabled binary variance penalties have essentially unchanged runtime. The complete `ShapRFECV.fit_compute()` benchmark changed from 361 to 347 ms, with overlapping timing ranges: this does **not** establish a reliable end-to-end feature-elimination speedup.

The interpreter timing covers report computation after a real model and explainer have been fitted. Benchmarks use nine calibrated timing batches, deterministic inputs, one native thread, and separate allocation measurements. This was a shared VM with scheduling noise. `docs/performance.md` records the experiments, limitations, environment, and reproduction commands; `scripts/benchmark_results/` contains raw final samples and output fingerprints. All eight benchmark report fingerprints match the baseline.

Regression tests preserve exact reported values, output dtypes, pandas tie ordering, duplicate labels, multiclass reductions, enabled penalties, and read-only/strided inputs. Disabled penalties also avoid NaN sort keys caused by overflow in an unused variance calculation for large finite SHAP values.

## Type of change

title: Add library typing and fix feature-elimination regressions
body:
## Description

Adds type hints to every function in the probatus library, checks function bodies with mypy, and ships `py.typed` for downstream users. Shared local/CI checks now enforce whole-package typing and static public-API contracts, including flag-dependent return types. Development dependencies include pandas stubs. Estimators and explainers use structural protocols; SHAP values and CV indices use concrete floating/integer array types. SHAP/plot options and boosting-fit parameters use typed dictionaries, and the abstract interfaces use generics. Explicit `Any` annotations are removed, with a Ruff rule preventing new imports; static API tests check typed dependency signatures and reject invalid model/option values.

Estimator protocols distinguish basic fitting from optional sample-weight support, including keyword-only weights. Fluent methods use `Self` to preserve subclass types. Input aliases use standard generic lists matching the accepted runtime containers, with independent element types for paired datasets, labels, weights, and groups. Independently typed estimator fixtures verify these contracts without inheriting sklearn classes.

- Fixes #278 by omitting `groups` when it is `None`, while continuing to pass real group labels into hyperparameter searches. Tests exercise GridSearchCV and RandomizedSearchCV with metadata routing enabled and disabled, verify group separation in inner and outer CV, and cover early stopping.
- Fixes #280 by retaining the whole-package coverage target already present on main, adding branch measurement and behavioral regression tests. Codecov uploads remain restricted to `main`; pull requests still collect whole-package coverage during tests. The fitted-state tests now actually invoke the guard instead of producing an unconditional xpass.
- Fixes #274 by honoring verbosity in LightGBM's early-stopping callback and replacing the tutorial's repeated timing runs with one actual early-stopping example. Both changed tutorials are executed with their outputs committed for the online documentation, including plots, tables, and printed feature-selection results. Model verbosity suppresses training logs at their source. It also explains model verbosity and scoped warning suppression.
- Confirms and incorporates the selection-policy bug reported in #277: coherent/parsimonious candidates must be within `best_mean - standard_error_threshold * best_std`. `best` still selects the highest mean score. Tests cover score scaling, negative scores, boundary inclusion, zero tolerance, and zero variance. The historical parameter name is retained and its standard-deviation semantics are documented.

Typing also exposed small input/return-path defects: the support-mask method was incorrectly static, ranking coerced feature names to integers, NumPy SHAP inputs accessed dataframe-only attributes, and Series conversion mishandled an omitted index. These are fixed with regression coverage.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fixes
- [x] Type-checking support
- [x] Documentation update

## Validation

- Shared `scripts/check.py`: lint, whole-package mypy/API contracts, complete unit suite (97 passed, 11 standard skips), and documentation build pass. Coverage is 92.1% of lines and 77.7% of branches; feature elimination is included. Native thread counts and CPU affinity were limited for local validation.
- Python 3.10 imports and type checking pass; the normal local environment is Python 3.12. Static fixtures cover estimators without sample weights, keyword-only weights, incompatible weight types, subclass-preserving fit returns, typed list inputs, and rejected unsupported containers.
- All 27 focused regression/helper tests pass with the minimum supported scikit-learn 1.4.2 and NumPy 1.26.4.
- Running the relevant regressions against the original methods produces eight expected failures, demonstrating coverage of the reported defects.
- Both changed feature-selection tutorials execute successfully (skipping only dependency installation in the already provisioned environment), with execution counts and all generated outputs saved. No LightGBM info logs are emitted. The documentation build preserves the saved plots, tables, and printed output.
- Wheel and source archive contain `py.typed`; static API checks pass against the installed wheel in an isolated downstream environment.

title: Fix sklearn API breakage when using search models with groups
body:
Fixes #278.

PR #275 added `groups=groups` to the search model's `.fit()` call (line 457). This breaks on sklearn 1.7+ where metadata routing is enabled by default - `RandomizedSearchCV.fit` and `GridSearchCV.fit` reject `groups` as an unexpected argument.

The fix reverts that call to `clone(self.model).fit(current_X, self.y)`. The `groups` parameter is only needed for the outer CV splits (lines 475/489), not for the inner hyperparameter search which runs its own internal CV.

Tested with sklearn 1.6.1 + metadata routing enabled manually, and all 25 feature_elimination tests pass.

title: fixed group CV in hyperparameter tuning
body:
While ShapRFECV was already compatible with group cross-validation (e.g., GroupKFold, LeaveOneGroupOut), hyperparameter tuning was not; even if a group cross-validation generator is passed to the hyperparameter tuner (e.g., GridSearchCV, RandomizedSearchCV, BayesSearchCV).

To correct this, `probatus/feature_elimination/feature_elimination.py` was modified to ensure the groups argument can be defined when calling both `fit()` and `fit_compute()` from `ShapRFECV`, and is actually passed into the model's `fit()` method. The change was done such that cross-validation schemes independent from data groups still work.

Ensuring groups are kept separate in training and validation data also during hyperparameter tuning is important in some applications, e.g., medical, to promote model parameters which robustly predict out-of-group samples.

Release notes

Sourced from numpy's releases.

v2.0.0

NumPy 2.0.0 Release Notes

NumPy 2.0.0 is the first major release since 2006. It is the result of 11 months of development since the last feature release and is the work of 212 contributors spread over 1078 pull requests. It contains a large number of exciting new features as well as changes to both the Python and C APIs.

This major release includes breaking changes that could not happen in a regular minor (feature) release - including an ABI break, changes to type promotion rules, and API changes which may not have been emitting deprecation warnings in 1.26.x. Key documents related to how to adapt to changes in NumPy 2.0, in addition to these release notes, include:

  • The numpy-2-migration-guide
  • The Numpy 2.0-specific advice in for downstream package authors

Highlights

Highlights of this release include:

  • New features:
    • A new variable-length string dtype, numpy.dtypes.StringDType and a new numpy.strings namespace with performant ufuncs for string operations,
    • Support for float32 and longdouble in all numpy.fft functions,
    • Support for the array API standard in the main numpy namespace.
  • Performance improvements:

title: Penalty on shap calculation for higher variance
body:
PR addresses #216 

**Overall objective:** Add penalty to features that has high variance in underlying shap values - when computing feature importance. This will (in theory) encourage selection of features that have more coherency across CV folds.

**API design:**
- Single parameter `shap_variance_penalty_factor` used to control enabling/disabling in addition to controlling the amount of penalty added to the mean(shap) computation. 
- Formula: `penalized_shap_abs_mean = (mean_shap - (std_shap * shap_variance_penalty_factor))`
- `shap_variance_penalty_factor` = None (default docstring)
- `shap_variance_penalty_factor`= 0 (same as None, no penalty)
- `shap_variance_penalty_factor`= 1 (one standard deviation of mean penalty)

**Work tasks:**
- [x] Add `shap_variance_penalty_factor` parameter to `ShapRFECV.fit`, `compute` & `fit_compute`
- [x] Update `EarlyStoppingShapRFECV.fit`, `compute` & `fit_compute`
- [x] Add `shap_variance_penalty_factor` to `shap_helpers.calculate_shap_importance`
- [x] Update `ShapModelInterpreter.fit`, `compute` & `fit_compute`
- [x] Add to doc strings throughout
- [x] Run simulation demonstrating impact of `shap_variance_penalty_factor` feature
- [x] Add unit tests
- [x] Add tutorial comparing RFECV methods and results as jupyter notebook

**Reviewers:** LMK any changes / improvements that can be made.

For 2, it could be disabled by either setting

title: Improve lightgbm logging and fix eval_metrics issue for lightgbm (EarlyStoppingShapRFECV)
body:
This is an improvement/addition to https://github.com/ing-bank/probatus/pull/164 (merged)

### Motivation
1. The `verbose` or `verbosity` parameter for `lightgbm` has been deprecated as of `lightgbm 3.3.0` together with `early_stopping_rounds`. We implemented the replacement solution (the `early_stopping` callback) for the latter deprecation in https://github.com/ing-bank/probatus/pull/164, but we did not take care of the validation logging/messages. At the moment these are, by default, logged/printed for every early stopping.
2. There is an issue for either `EarlyStoppingShapRFECV` or `lightgbm` where the specified `eval_metric` isn't used and the validation defaults to the scoring/loss instead.

### Solution
1. We can use the `lightgbm` `log_evaluation` callback and set the `period=0`. This means the early stopping validation won't be printed, but it is a static solution.
2. We can set `first_metric_only=True` in the `early_stopping` callback, which will only use the first metric, but is a surefire solution to using the specified `eval_metric`. Downside is that this is again a static solution.

*Both solutions are specific and static for `lightgbm` models*

title: Add util function to get SHAP values via CV
body:
# Motivation

SHAP values provide an excellent way to estimate model feature importance. The SHAP values tell us how much a feature contributes to (impacts) the model prediction.

When we evaluate model performance, we typically want to know the performance on different data sets:

* train
* validation (val)
* test

Similarly, when we calculate SHAP values, we want to know the impact of the features when the model is applied to different data sets.

With the current `shap` API, it is straightforward to calculate SHAP values for train, val, and test sets.

However, most modeling problems involve limited data, so designating both a val and test set is unacceptable, because too little data is left to train the model. Enter cross validation, of course, where there is no hold-out val set, but the validation occurs via CV on the train set.

With the current `shap` API, there is no support for calculating SHAP values via CV (e.g. by integration with `sklearn`).

So we have three options:

* Calculate SHAP values on train. But this is as flawed as evaluating model performance on train alone. You will get the importance of features of a model trained and evaluated on the same data, i.e. it is not a fair evaluation.
* Calculate SHAP values on test. This seems like a better choice, but if we are calculating SHAP values as a way of selecting model features, it seems a dangerous choice. Ideally, modeling decisions should never be based on the hold-out test set -- that's why we have val sets and CV after all.
* Calculate SHAP values on train via CV. Sounds ideal! But how?
This PR provides a helper function to calculate SHAP values via CV.

Possible contribution to `probatus.utils.shap_helpers` if `probatus` maintainers see value and agree.

`ShapRFECV` is still the better option overall, but for some users a recursive approach may not be feasible due to computational cost. With `get_shap_cv_value`, user gets the benefit of CV in a non-recursive approach and can then select the `n` top features in more confidence.
